messages:
sara: FYI customer acme-inc reports sudden p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings since last night
joel: which region and model?
sara: eu-west, embed-large, started ~2023-11-08T02:10Z after our nightly infra update
anyA: (checking) looks correlated with the 02:00 CUDA/driver rollout to dedicated pools
lena: I can see p95 ~200ms -> 800ms and p99 from 700ms -> 2.3s on the embed route in eu-west-2 metrics
marc-oncall: tagging infra: @joel @lena can you triage? customer on a paid SLO, opened support ticket #4321
joel: looking at node-level traces now. initial hypothesis: storage queue depth on a subset of nodes + driver scheduling change
infra-bot: added alert: host.io.util high on pool-dedicated-eu2-*-nvme (avg queue depth > 4 for bursts)
support-bot: customer message: "we see a spike in latency and some 500s for embeds, started after maintenance"
anya: any auth/billing errors? could be unrelated
sara: support logs show no auth/billing failures, only increased latency and occasional 504s at the API layer
lena: dumping iostat from one affected node (nvme):
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device:            r/s     w/s   rsec/s   wsec/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1          12.00  110.00  48000.00  360000.00  3000.00     2.90    9.2    1.3   10.5   0.12  92.00
```
joel: that avgqu-sz ~2.9 is suspicious for our small request sizes, and %util 92% under typical load looks saturated
anya: check dmesg for NVMe driver errors and GPU firmware messages
joel: dmesg extract from same host: 
```
[Nov08 02:03:11] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x3f failed, status: 0x04
[Nov08 02:03:12] nvidia: GPU0: scheduling hiccup after driver v530.12
[Nov08 02:03:13] nvme nvme0: reset controller
```
lena: ok so two things: nvme resets around the same time as the driver rollout, and kernel logs show GPU scheduling messages. could be driver interaction causing IO amplification
marc-oncall: can we repro locally in staging? any canary nodes upgraded?
joel: canary pool eu-west-canary was on older driver and didn't show spikes. upgrade batch included dedicated-eu2-worker pool with mixed firmware levels -> affected nodes are subset with older NVMe firmware + new driver combo
anya: that pattern matches previous regression where driver I/O path changed retries -> queue depth amplified
sara: customer impact: p99 embeddings up, some inference requests timed out -> support offered partial credits, but we need mitigation asap
lena: short-term mitigations we can apply now: 1) route embed requests away from affected pool -> fallback routing to hosted/other region 2) reduce batch size and max concurrency on affected nodes 3) emergency rollback of driver on affected dedicated pool 4) throttle background host maintenance IO
joel: routing change: add node selector to embed route to prefer pools with driver version < 530.12, can push traffic within 5m
marc-oncall: we should do routing + batching first, rollback only if still bad. rollback needs coordination with infra and customers on Dedicated contracts
anya: quick command to reduce max concurrency on the node:
```
kubectl -n inference patch ds inference-worker --type='json' -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"4" } ]'
```
joel: I pushed rate limit and concurrency change to pool-dedicated-eu2-*-nvme, reduced batch sizes by 30% and max_inflight=4
lena: after change metrics already show p95 dropped to 300ms and p99 to 1.1s on affected nodes (10m post-change)
marc-oncall: good. support: can you inform customer and offer temporary routing to eu-central until we fully mitigate? mention the temporary change and ETA for rollback assessment
sara: done, customer accepted routing to eu-central and appreciates the quick action :thumbsup:
anya: next steps: 1) schedule driver rollback on affected pool tonight if metrics don't fully stabilize 2) open firmware upgrade plan for NVMe on older hosts 3) run repro script to confirm root cause and collect kernel+nvme logs for vendor escalation
joel: repro steps to collect from a node:
```
# start load generator
./scripts/bench_embed.sh --concurrency 8 --batch 64
# collect iostat and dmesg while load runs
iostat -x 1 60 > /tmp/iostat.log
dmesg -w > /tmp/dmesg.log &
# collect nvme logs
nvme-cli log-subsys -s all > /tmp/nvme_log.txt
```
lena: filed advisory with hw vendor and CC'd reliability team. opened issue INF-1724 with logs and timeline
marc-oncall: assigning owners: joel (rollback plan + canary rollback), anya (vendor escalation + firmware plan), lena (metric dashboards + postmortem), sara (customer comms + billing follow-up)
joel: will prepare rollback playbook, if rollback is needed we'll coordinate a short maintenance window for that pool
anya: vendor asked for nvme_log.txt, dmesg snippets, and kernel version. collecting now
sara: support ticket updated, customer routed, credits pending until final RCA
infra-bot: mitigation checklist: routing applied, concurrency reduced, alert thresholds adjusted, rollback pending
marc-oncall: we should keep thread open until RCA. nice work team, lets target a short postmortem within 48h

sara: quick note — if rollback not possible, we might need to proactively place affected hosts into maintenance and autoscale capacity in unaffected pools to absorb traffic
joel: acknowledged. I'll post an ETA for the rollback playbook in 30m
anya: collecting remaining logs and will upload to INF-1724 in the next 20m
lena: monitoring shows last 15m p99 trending down to ~900ms, still elevated but acceptable as temporary
marc-oncall: closing loop: keep updates here. thanks all."
